Adjusted assessment incorporating the Beige Book and SLOOS:
- Policy stance: The FOMC held the target range at 5.25–5.50% and continued QT, emphasizing data dependence and vigilance on inflation—hawkish but not escalating.
- Beige Book overlay (District Reports ahead of the Sep 20, 2023 meeting): Activity described as modest rather than solid; consumer spending mixed (goods softer, services/travel relatively firm), manufacturing flat-to-down, CRE weak—especially office—with subdued residential activity; labor markets still tight but easing with slower job gains and moderating wage growth; price increases continued to slow but remained elevated; banks reported tighter lending standards, softer loan demand, and rising deposit competition, with some uptick in delinquencies from low levels.
- SLOOS overlay: Broad-based tightening across consumer and real estate credit (CRE and RRE, HELOCs, credit cards, autos) and weaker demand, corroborating tighter credit conditions and pointing to a more material drag on growth and hiring ahead.
- Net: Compared with the statement’s “solid pace,” the Beige Book and SLOOS indicate softer momentum and tighter credit, reinforcing downside risks to activity and employment, while inflation pressures persist but are moderating. Overall tilt shifts more cautious than the headline FOMC tone.
